text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi regained his post as vice president of the dominant United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), after losing it in the last UMNO elections in 1993.

-- Croatia's Ambassador to Malaysia, Kresimir Znidaric has been called back to his home country by President Franjo Tudjman, after being accused of allegedly raping a 27-year old Filipino maid, Maria Fe Ocampo. Ocampo had filed a lawsuit in Kuala Lumpur against the ambassador on Thursday.

-- The 1997 Budget is unlikely to be an expansionary one, according to a report by a local securities research house. The report said that direct taxes were unlikely to come down immediately, but would be reduced over the next four years. The report said that the company anticipates import duties to be reduced in line with international trade agreements.

-- Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi attributed part of the credit for his historic comeback as UMNO vice president, to party leader and Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad. "The (UMNO) president's speech may have paved the way for my return," he said.

-- The Malaysian cabinet would not be reshuffled after the changes in the UMNO party's governing line-up following the elections over the last two days, said Mahathir. Four cabinet ministers lost their positions in the UMNO hierarchy.
